newsitem.title: FRANCE: Total sees lower oil prices in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Total sees lower oil prices in 1997.

text.p: Total SA chairman Thierry Desmarest said on Wednesday he expected the price of Brent crude oil to ease in the rest of 1997 from the current level of just below $23 per barrel due to increased production by oil exporting countries.
He said he did not believe the oil price would fall as far as $16.40 as seen in the 1994/1995 period.
"I do not think that we will continue to see the favourable prices from the start of the year," Desmarest said. "But it is very unlikely that it will return to a level of $16.40 per barrel."

The $16.40 level is part of Total's reference for improving its profitability to 10 percent of equity in 1998 and 12 percent in 2000. In 1996 the company had a return on equity of 10.3 percent but Desmarest said that using the reference values, the return on equity for 1996 would have been 8.4 percent.
He said that the return on equity for 1997 would be higher than the nine percent target for the year based on the reference values.
